Sumi.$description: 墨 — Ink Black. Foundation of all ukiyoe. Used since 1670.

Beni.$description: 紅 — Crimson. Safflower pigment, defining color of benizuri-e (1740–).

Midori.$description: 緑 — Green. First appeared in benizuri-e as complementary to beni.

Kin.$description: 金/茶 — Gold / Ochre. Metallic pigment prominent in nishiki-e polychrome prints.

Ao.$description: 青灰 — Blue-gray. First appeared in refined benizuri-e, expanded in nishiki-e.

Ai.$description: 藍 — Indigo. Deep plant-based blue, introduced in large-format nishiki-e (1770–).

Bero.$description: ベロ藍 — Prussian Blue. Imported synthetic pigment, iconic in Hokusai & Hiroshige landscapes (1800–).

Gin.$description: 銀灰 — Mica Gray. Crushed mica (kirazuri) used by Utamaro and Sharaku (1790–).

Hada.$description: 肌/紙 — Warm Paper. The washi substrate visible as background and skin tone.
